hypothesis: A different part size, thread count or transfer engine for the parallel ranged GETs into the memfd raises the cold weight-download throughput above P1's 79 MiB/s, and changes nothing after the download.

hypotheses.ldr: A/A check: P1's own loader, run from the E3 zip through e3_entry, downloads as fast as the control (the wrapper and the bigger zip cost nothing).
hypotheses.aa: P1's setting (64 MiB x 32 threads) re-implemented with request counters downloads as fast as P1's loader.
hypotheses.t16x64: Smaller parts (16 MiB) on more threads (64) raise download throughput.
hypotheses.t8x128: 8 MiB parts on 128 threads raise download throughput.
hypotheses.t32x64: 32 MiB parts on 64 threads raise download throughput.
hypotheses.t64x64: More threads (64) at P1's part size raise download throughput.
hypotheses.crt8: awscrt's S3Client (8 MiB parts, 25 Gbit/s target), writing each body chunk into the memfd from its callback, beats the boto3 thread pool.
hypotheses.crt16: awscrt's S3Client (16 MiB parts, 25 Gbit/s target), writing each body chunk into the memfd from its callback, beats the boto3 thread pool.
